title: Dedicated pool capacity ghosting - lab notes
content:
Goal: rapid breadcrumbs for the ""ghosting"" capacity issue that keeps reappearing on dedicated pools (pool-d, pool-e). This is a scratchpad — raw commands, observations, and hypotheses.

Summary of observed behavior:
- Pools intermittently report 'available capacity' in Console but tasks still queue for 20-120s.
- Autoscaler sometimes spins up nodes but they cycle out (preempt/killed) before becoming fully warm (model loading / KV cache).
- Symptoms repeat after rolling restarts of the control plane or after overnight quiet periods.
- Error spikes correlated with short bursts of traffic (10-30 requests/s) and large model loads (~8k context).

Timeline / quick logs (local times UTC):
2026-02-28 09:12 - First alert: route=prod/dedicated-a high queue depth. Console shows 2 healthy nodes, but tracer shows per-request latency spike to 3.2s.
2026-02-28 09:14 - kubectl to check pods: 
$ kubectl get pods -n rw-dedicated --selector=pool=pool-d -o wide
--> STATUS: Running, RESTARTS: 0, NODE: gke-pool-d-02
2026-02-28 09:15 - Describe failing task: 
$ kubectl logs model-server-abc -n rw-dedicated | tail -n 50
--> "WARN: kvcache miss for prefix id=0x3a2"
--> "ERROR: failed to mmap weights: errno=12 (Cannot allocate memory)"
2026-02-28 09:17 - HPA/Scaler snapshot: 
$ curl -sS http://autoscaler.internal/api/v1/metrics?pool=pool-d | jq .
--> recorded scale-up request, policy=min_nodes=2,max_nodes=10,target_util=0.65
--> decision: scale_up to 3 nodes, created instance id i-0fca...
2026-02-28 09:20 - New node boots, but kubelet reports GCE preemption shortly after (preempted by OVERRIDE). Node terminates at 09:23.

Commands tried (notes + results):
- kubectl describe pod <model-server> -> shows image pull + model copy start, then OOM on mmap (weird, GPUs should be used).
- nvidia-smi inside container -> sometimes empty or "No devices were found" during transient states. Suggests driver mismatch or node eviction before driver finishing.
- journalctl -u rw-agent -> repeated "Failed to attach GPU device: resource not found" messages.
- curl -X POST to autoscaler force-scale endpoint: returned 202 but new node replaced after 3m with reason "preempted by scheduler".
- Prometheus queries: 
  - max_over_time(node_gpu_util[10m]) shows short peaks but avg low.
  - rate(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total[5m]) aligns with node churn spikes.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Node preemption + late model-loading: Preemptible instances or spot reclaim happens after node registers but before model fully loaded (KV cache and mmap). The autoscaler thinks capacity exists (node counted as Ready) but actual serving processes not warmed.
   - Evidence: node shows Ready, pods Running, but nvidia-smi reports no devices or processes killed.
   - Test: force new nodes to non-preemptible type temporarily + reproduce.
2) Race between load balancer routing and container readiness: readinessProbe passes too early (port handshake okay) while model load is still in progress. Router begins sending traffic and pushes memory / GPU allocation into transient failure.
   - Evidence: readinessProbe configured as tcp-check on 8080. Logs show model copy after readiness.
   - Test: change readinessProbe to query /health/warm which checks model loaded + KV cache > 50% or sequence length warm.
3) Autoscaler accounting mismatch (ghost nodes): scaling decision counts nodes in provisioning but they don't reach warm state; autoscaler circuit thinks capacity satisfied so it throttles new scale-ups.
   - Evidence: autoscaler metrics show "nodes_provisioning" reported but "nodes_ready_for_traffic" lags by ~40s.
   - Test: instrument autoscaler to separate "ready_for_traffic" metric and trigger immediate additional scale if warm-ready < expected.
4) Kernel/drivers failing to bind during heavy boot storms: kernel log shows sporadic "failed to bind kernel module" errors correlated with GC/IO storms at boot causing driver timeouts.
   - Evidence: journalctl has intermittent "nvidia: probe failed" lines.
   - Test: boot slower, add driver init delay or pre-baked driver image.

Quick experiments run so far and outcomes:
- Experiment: forced non-preemptible instance type for pool-d for 1h test.
  Result: latency spikes reduced; model servers reached warm state in 18-22s vs previously 35-90s. No preemption events. Encouraging.
- Experiment: changed readinessProbe to include /health/warm on canary nodes.
  Result: Routing delayed until model load finished -> queue depth spikes avoided but global capacity reported lower. Behavior suggests readiness gate is effective.
- Experiment: manually increased autoscaler target to 5 during traffic burst.
  Result: additional nodes provisioned but 2 nodes terminated within 2-3m with "OOM mmap" in logs. Suspect memory accounting/descriptors burned by multi-process startup.

Actionable next steps (short):
- Rollout warm-readiness probe to one more pool (pool-e) for next 24h. (owner: Lina)
- Run 2-hour test with non-preemptible nodes on a single cluster to confirm preemption hypothesis (owner: Samir).
- Add metric "nodes_warm_ready" to autoscaler and alert when warm_ready < desired_nodes by >1 for 2m. (owner: me/Aisha)
- Reproduce OOM: create minimal repro that loads same model weight size with same mmap flags on a test instance type. Collect strace/journal. (owner: me)

Longer-term ideas:
- Autoscaler semantics: add "provisioning" vs "warm" states, have router prefer warm nodes. Fallback policy: route to hosted models when warm_ready < threshold.
- Image bake with driver+model cache snapshot to reduce warm time (prebake weights to ephemeral image layer).
- Improve node lifecycle hooks: prevent marking node Ready until gpu plugin confirms device available and driver modules bound.

Notes to self / loose threads:
- Check cloud provider reclaim window details (GCP preemptible vs spot interruption notice length).
- Compare mmap flags used by model loader vs recommended for huge pages - maybe fragmentation cause.
- Examine kernel dmesg around "failed to mmap weights" for mapping: out of memory vs permission denied.
- Isolate whether mmap OOM is inside container cgroup vs host OOM.

Errors to grep for in logs:
- "failed to mmap weights"
- "Failed to attach GPU device"
- "nvidia: probe failed"
- "No devices were found"
- "node terminated: preempted"

Helpful commands (copy-paste):
- kubectl get pods -n rw-dedicated --selector=pool=pool-d -o wide
- kubectl logs -n rw-dedicated <pod> --previous
- kubectl describe node <node-name> | egrep "Taints|Conditions|Allocated resources|Preemption" -A5
- gcloud compute instances describe <instance-id> --project=redwood-prod --format=json | jq '.status, .scheduling'
- curl -sS http://autoscaler.internal/api/v1/state?pool=pool-d | jq .

Open questions for next sync:
- Do we accept slightly slower cold-starts in exchange for lower churn (non-preemptible baseline)?
- Is there a cost-optimized middle ground (longer-lived spot with warm-cache snapshot)?
- Should readiness semantics be part of the SLO definition for the Dedicated product?

TL;DR: Strong signals that preemption + early readiness + mmap/memory races are the root causes. Short-term mitigations (warm health probe and non-preemptible test) show promise. Need to add explicit "warm-ready" accounting in autoscaler and tighten node readiness gating.

End of notes. Will update as experiments complete.
